claims.text: High configurational entropy intrinsically promotes a single-phase structure in high-entropy nanoalloys.
High configurational entropy causes sluggish atomic diffusion in high-entropy nanoalloys.
A single-phase structure and sluggish diffusion collectively inhibit phase separation during prolonged high-temperature exposure.
A single-phase structure and sluggish diffusion collectively inhibit chemical segregation during prolonged high-temperature exposure.
The proposed starting material is a near-equiatomic nanoalloy with a homogeneous, single-phase microstructure and nanometer-sized grains.
The nanoalloy will be annealed at approximately 800°C for about 10 hours under an inert or vacuum atmosphere.
An inert or vacuum atmosphere will prevent oxidation during annealing.
High configurational entropy thermodynamically stabilizes the single-phase microstructure.
Reduced atomic mobility delays or prevents the development of chemical inhomogeneity at high temperature.
Reduced atomic mobility delays or prevents phase decomposition at high temperature.
After annealing, the high-entropy nanoalloy will show less phase segregation than the conventional control.
After annealing, the high-entropy nanoalloy will show less grain growth than the conventional control.
After annealing, the high-entropy nanoalloy will retain a more uniform chemical composition than the conventional control.
Conventional low-entropy or multiphase nanoalloys undergo significant phase separation, chemical segregation, or grain coarsening during extended high-temperature annealing.
The prediction is restricted to nanoalloys with nanometer-scale grains and constituents selected to produce high mixing entropy.
The prediction applies only below the alloy melting point and in atmospheres that do not induce oxidation or other chemical reactions.
Element-specific diffusion kinetics, intermetallic formation tendencies, and grain-boundary characteristics may alter the expected sluggish-diffusion behavior.
XRD, TEM, and EDS mapping can respectively assess phase constitution, grain morphology, and elemental-distribution uniformity before and after annealing.
